Boc deprotection of piperazine nitrogen with TFA/DCM
Urea coupling of free piperazine nitrogen with DBCO-amine (CDI-mediated carbonylation)
Installation of the primary amine conjugation handle via reductive amination or Boc-deprotection of the cyclohexyl terminal amine
NHS-ester or maleimide activation of the terminal amine for antibody or siRNA conjugation as needed
expected_failure_modes: 8-step linear synthesis reduces overall yield and scalability, increasing cost-of-goods for clinical development
Low Tanimoto similarity (0.152) to validated MCC linker suggests uncertain translational relevance and potential for unexpected PK behavior
Dual urea bonds and piperazine ring may reduce aqueous solubility despite the polar groups, causing aggregation of siRNA-ADC conjugates
DBCO moiety may undergo non-specific thiol-yne side reactions with serum albumin cysteine-34, leading to premature payload loss in circulation
validation_experiments: DAR analysis by HIC and native SEC-MALS to assess conjugation homogeneity and confirm DAR2 preference consistent with sulfo-SMCC benchmark
Plasma stability assay (human, mouse, 37°C, 7 days) with LC-MS/MS quantification of intact conjugate vs free siRNA
Solubility and aggregation assessment by DLS and analytical SEC at physiological pH and ionic strength
In vitro gene silencing potency (RT-qPCR) of siRNA-linker-antibody conjugate vs naked siRNA and sulfo-SMCC-linked control in target-expressing cells
narrative.information_gain: Testing this molecule would reveal whether replacing the classical maleimide-thiol chemistry (sulfo-SMCC) with a DBCO-SPAAC click handle on a rigid bis-urea scaffold can maintain or improve DAR2 homogeneity and silencing potency for siRNA-ADCs, thereby expanding the conjugation chemistry toolbox beyond thiol-maleimide for oligonucleotide payloads.

narrative.design_rationale: This linker satisfies the non-cleavable-rigid design rule for siRNA payloads by incorporating a fused bipyrimidine-dihydroisoindole core that enforces conformational rigidity, minimizing entropic penalties during conjugation and promoting homogeneous DAR species. The DBCO handle enables strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition (SPAAC) with azide-functionalized siRNA, providing a bioorthogonal, non-cleavable triazole linkage that ensures high serum stability consistent with the high stability priority. The terminal amine on the cyclohexane spacer allows antibody conjugation via NHS-ester chemistry, while the rigid aromatic scaffold maintains appropriate spatial separation between antibody and siRNA payload.
synthesis_route: Suzuki coupling of 5-bromopyrimidine-2-carboxylic acid with 5-(4,4,5,5-tetramethyl-1,3,2-dioxaborolan-2-yl)pyrimidine-2-amine to form the bipyrimidine core
Buchwald-Hartley N-arylation of the 2-aminopyrimidine with 2-ethynyl-iodobenzene to install the alkyne-aniline moiety
Intramolecular copper-catalyzed cyclization to form the dihydroisoindole ring bearing the internal alkyne (DBCO-like handle)
Amide coupling of the pyrimidine carboxylic acid with trans-4-aminocyclohexylamine (mono-Boc protected) using HATU/DIPEA
Boc deprotection with TFA to reveal the terminal primary amine conjugation handle
expected_failure_modes: Poor aqueous solubility of the extended aromatic scaffold may limit conjugation efficiency with hydrophilic siRNA in aqueous buffers, unlike the sulfo-SMCC benchmark which carries a solubilizing sulfonate
The internal alkyne in the DBCO-like moiety may undergo non-specific thiol-yne reactions with cysteine residues on the antibody or serum proteins
Rigid bipyrimidine core may be susceptible to CYP-mediated oxidative metabolism at the electron-rich nitrogen positions, reducing in vivo stability
Low Tanimoto similarity (0.16) to clinical MCC linker suggests unpredictable pharmacokinetic behavior with limited translational precedent
validation_experiments: SPAAC conjugation kinetics with azide-modified siRNA monitored by HPLC and MALDI-TOF to confirm click efficiency and DAR distribution (target DAR2)
Plasma stability assay in human and mouse plasma at 37°C over 7 days with LC-MS/MS quantification of intact conjugate vs. free siRNA
Hydrophobic interaction chromatography (HIC) and SEC of the full ADC to assess DAR homogeneity and aggregation propensity
Kinetic solubility measurement of the linker-payload intermediate in PBS (pH 7.4) and conjugation buffer to identify solubility-limited reaction conditions
narrative.information_gain: Testing this linker will reveal whether a fully rigid, extended aromatic DBCO-type scaffold can match or exceed sulfo-SMCC's conjugation homogeneity for siRNA payloads despite lacking an explicit solubilizing group, thereby decoupling the contributions of rigidity versus hydrophilicity to DAR2 selectivity.

economics.note: order-of-magnitude heuristics from step count + stability; not a quote

narrative.design_rationale: This linker satisfies the non-cleavable-rigid design rule for oligonucleotide payloads by incorporating a DBCO click-chemistry handle for strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddation (SPAAC) conjugation, ensuring stable triazole linkage that is non-cleavable in circulation. Rigidity is enforced through the fused dibenzocyclooctyne (DBCO) core and the sulfonamide-piperazine backbone, mimicking the beneficial rigidity of sulfo-SMCC that maximized DAR2 homogeneity in literature precedent. The sulfonamide moiety enhances aqueous solubility analogous to the sulfo group in SMCC, which is critical for maintaining compatibility with hydrophilic siRNA payloads while preserving high plasma stability (score 1.0, no identified liabilities).
synthesis_route: Synthesis of 4-aminocyclohexyl amine core via reductive amination or Boc-protection/deprotection of trans-1,4-diaminocyclohexane
Sulfonylation of cyclohexylamine nitrogen with piperazine-1-sulfonyl chloride to install the sulfonamide-piperazine unit
Amide coupling of piperazine nitrogen with 6-chloronicotinoyl chloride or activated ester (HATU/DIPEA)
SNAr displacement of chloropyridine with DBCO-amine (5H-dibenzo[b,f]azocine secondary amine) to install the DBCO click handle
Global deprotection and purification by reverse-phase HPLC to yield the final bifunctional linker
expected_failure_modes: DBCO moiety may undergo premature reaction with biological thiols or nucleophiles in formulation buffer, reducing conjugation efficiency
The extended aromatic DBCO system may increase lipophilicity beyond optimal range, causing aggregation of the siRNA-linker-antibody conjugate
Sulfonamide bond may be susceptible to slow hydrolysis under acidic endosomal conditions (pH 5.0), potentially compromising non-cleavable design intent
Rigid piperazine-sulfonamide-cyclohexane spacer may impose steric constraints that reduce SPAAC reaction kinetics with azide-modified siRNA
validation_experiments: DAR analysis by HIC and native SEC-MALS after SPAAC conjugation with azide-functionalized siRNA to assess conjugation efficiency and homogeneity
Plasma stability assay (human, mouse, 37°C, 7 days) with LC-MS/MS quantification of intact conjugate vs. free siRNA release
SPAAC reaction kinetics measurement (second-order rate constant) by monitoring DBCO absorbance loss at 309 nm with model azide-siRNA
Hydrophobicity assessment by HIC retention time comparison against sulfo-SMCC-based conjugate and aggregation propensity by SEC
narrative.information_gain: Testing this DBCO-based rigid non-cleavable linker will reveal whether replacing the traditional thiol-maleimide conjugation chemistry (sulfo-SMCC) with bioorthogonal SPAAC click chemistry can maintain or improve DAR2 homogeneity and plasma stability for siRNA ADCs, while informing whether the added rigidity and steric bulk of the dibenzocyclooctyne system is tolerable for this payload class.
